title: Every Load comes from the repository

statements.says: Loop turns auto-memory off with autoMemoryEnabled: false in the repository's .claude/settings.json, so every Load comes from a file the repository carries.
skillworks-setup writes the same line into every repository it configures.
A developer who wants memory back in one repository writes it into .claude/settings.local.json, which is per-machine and never committed.
The memory files stay on disk, so removing the line is one commit and the files the machine already holds come back with it.
The preflight script warns when the line is missing, and warns rather than fails.
Memory files are Loads whose source is the machine rather than the repository, so one commit steers two machines differently and a run cannot be read back from what the repository holds.
The project settings line beats a developer's own toggle, because /config writes auto-memory to the user's settings and the project file wins.
skillworks-setup leaves settings.local.json alone because a conflict there can only be deliberate.
The preflight warns rather than fails because a team that removed the line on purpose should not have their loop stop.
A developer's own settings were rejected, because they reach every repository on one machine and none on any other, and the project settings win over them anyway.
A managed policy file was rejected for now, because the rollout has to stay small and reversible and a policy is neither; it stays available the day the company wants the line locked.
The plugin was rejected, because a plugin is not one of the settings sources Claude Code reads and only ships skills.
